persona: Maintenance Coordinator (MAINT_COORDINATOR / MAINTENANCE_COORDINATOR), first day, 13-inch laptop (~1280x800), district maintenance office. Knows the job: new field reports arrive, I look at where they are, decide whether they belong to something already happening, and send them on (assessment / no assessment / ask reporter / duplicate). Has never seen ERIS and had no training. After sign-in lands on /my-work (web/src/pages/LoginPage.tsx:42); header shows the raw role code 'MAINT_COORDINATOR' (web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:157); sidebar offers Workspace > My Work, Operations > Mission Center / Event Groups / Incidents / Assessments, GIS Tools > Terrain Cross Sections, Account > Settings (web/src/ui/AppShell.tsx:79-102).

tasks.task: Find the new field reports waiting for me today and accept one into ERIS with the right Event Group and disposition
steps: Sign in; land on /my-work with the heading 'My Work' and 'N items waiting on your role' (web/src/features/myWork/MyWorkPage.tsx:120-123).

Scan the left rail: each card reads 'Triage · Incident #12', a title or 'Field report', a red 'New report' pill, and 'D3 · Placer · R080 · PM 12.30 · Reported Sep 5, 2026, 7:10 AM' (MyWorkPage.tsx:152-155). Newest report is on top (sort by first_observed_at desc, MyWorkPage.tsx:68-71). There is no date or district filter, so 'today' means reading the 'Reported' timestamps.

First card is auto-selected (MyWorkPage.tsx:88); the right panel shows 'FIELD REPORT #12 — NOT YET IN THE INCIDENT RECORD', title, location + 6-decimal lat/lon + Reported time, 'Awaiting triage' pill, the description, an 'Open incident record' button, and a blue 'NEXT STEP  Waiting on Maintenance Coordinator' card with 'Start triage' (web/src/features/myWork/TriageWorkItem.tsx:55-79).

Want to see photos / reporter before deciding: click 'Open incident record' -> /incidents/12, which is just the Incidents table with the row highlighted on the 'Awaiting intake' tab (web/src/features/incidents/IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:102-112, 294-298); no photos, no reporter, no detail page. Browser Back to My Work.

Click 'Start triage' (TriageWorkItem.tsx:73-79). Modal 'Event Group review — incident #12' opens with 'Confirm shared-event context before triage…' (web/src/features/eventGroups/EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:167-168).

Left column: 'Nearby open Event Groups' + radius select (default 25 miles), first radio 'Starts its own event', then radio rows like 'Hwy 80 Emigrant Gap slides' / '#4 · D3 · Placer · R080 · PM 10.80 · 3 incidents · 1.5 mi away' (EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:180-198). The nearest group is already pre-selected (EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:92-94). Right column: 380px map with red dot (new report), blue dots (groups), red diamonds (selected group's incidents) and a legend (web/src/features/eventGroups/EventGroupTriageMap.tsx:86-134).
Decide: keep the pre-selected group, or click 'Starts its own event' (title auto-filled 'Route 080 · PM 12.30 · Placer Event Group'). Optionally type a 'Coordinator note'.

Click the outlined button 'Record decision · use selected Event Group' (or 'Create Event Group and record decision') (EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:208-210). Status line changes to 'Decision recorded: <title>' (line 211). Only now does 'Continue to triage' enable (line 237).

Click 'Continue to triage'. Second modal 'Triage incident #12' with a three-sentence policy paragraph, green 'Event Group decision recorded for this coordinator review.', 'DISPOSITION' select (default 'Assessment required'), a grey consequence line, 'DECISION NOTES' textarea, buttons 'Review Event Group again' / 'Cancel' / 'Record triage decision' (web/src/features/incidents/IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:82-108).

Pick the disposition (four options: Assessment required / No assessment required / Needs reporter information / Duplicate or linked, IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:18-23), add notes, click 'Record triage decision'.

Dialog closes; item leaves the rail; green notice 'Incident #12 accepted — assessment #7 routed for office delegation.' appears at the top (TriageWorkItem.tsx:38-41; MyWorkPage.tsx:128, 177). Next report is auto-selected.

frictionPoints.step: Landing on My Work and reading the rail
frictionPoints.problem: The queue never says which district it is, and there is no district/date filter; the coordinator has to trust that 'items waiting on your role' equals 'my district's new reports today'.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The client just fetches /incidents?limit=1000 and keeps current_stage === COORDINATOR_REVIEW (MyWorkPage.tsx:59-60); nothing on screen names the district or the day. A newcomer expects 'District 3 intake — 4 new today', not a role-generic count, and cannot tell whether reports from another district would also land here.

frictionPoints.step: Reading the same state three ways
frictionPoints.problem: The rail says 'New report', the panel pill says 'Awaiting triage', the eyebrow says 'not yet in the incident record', and the Incidents page calls the same thing 'Awaiting intake'.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Four labels for one state (MyWorkPage.tsx:153; TriageWorkItem.tsx:55,59; IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:223). A first-day user assumes different words mean different states and wonders if 'triage' and 'intake' are separate steps.

frictionPoints.problem: The triage panel shows only title, description, D/C/R/PM, coordinates and time — no photos, no reporter name/phone, no incident type, no road-inventory match. 'Open incident record' leads to a table row, not a record.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The job decision (assessment vs no assessment vs duplicate) is made from photos and who called it in. TriageWorkItem.tsx:52-65 surfaces none of it and /incidents/:id only highlights a row in the Incidents table (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:102-112); there is no incident detail page on the web at all. The coordinator either guesses or opens the mobile app.

frictionPoints.step: Clicking 'Start triage' and seeing 'Event Group review' first
frictionPoints.problem: The first thing asked is an 'Event Group' decision, a term the coordinator has never heard; the job vocabulary is 'location', 'site' or (mobile) 'Project'.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:167-168 and 180 use 'Event Group' with no definition. The mobile triage picker calls the same object a 'Project'. The dialog description 'Confirm shared-event context before triage' is abstract; a newcomer does not know whether they are grouping by storm, by slope, by route segment or by work order.

frictionPoints.problem: A radio for the nearest group within 25 miles is already checked when the dialog opens, so pressing the buttons without reading attaches the report to whatever happens to be closest.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:92-94 sets selectedId to nearby.items[0]. 25 miles of I-80 spans several unrelated slides; the pre-selection reads as 'the system already matched it' and the coordinator defers to it. Nothing says 'suggested' or 'nearest' on the checked row.

frictionPoints.step: Trying to continue after choosing a group
frictionPoints.problem: The obvious primary button 'Continue to triage' is disabled; the user must first press the outlined secondary-looking 'Record decision · use selected Event Group'. The only hint is 12px grey text 'Record the decision to continue to triage.'
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: A two-button commit for one choice (EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:208-211, 237). Disabled buttons give no tooltip. Newcomers click Continue, nothing happens, click Cancel thinking the dialog is broken. Also 'Record decision' saves to the server immediately with no undo (lines 140-146), before they have decided the disposition.

frictionPoints.problem: Policy sentences about 'incident classification remains unassigned' and 'the permanent Incident key is minted only when the coordinator approves and forwards' appear above the form on every triage.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:85. 'Key minting' and 'classification' are database/engineering concepts, not coordinator concepts. The newcomer wonders whether they must do something about the key.

frictionPoints.problem: 'Disposition' defaults to 'Assessment required' — the most consequential option — and one click on 'Record triage decision' commits it with no confirmation.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: TriageWorkItem.tsx:75 presets ASSESSMENT_REQUIRED; IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:106 commits immediately. 'Disposition' is jargon (the button says 'decision', the notes field says 'Decision notes'). A first-day user who just wants to 'accept the report' will accept-and-route-to-GeoTech every time without realising a second office has been engaged.

frictionPoints.step: Choosing 'Duplicate or linked' or 'Needs reporter information'
frictionPoints.problem: Neither option asks for the target incident or for which fields the reporter should fix; there is only the free-text notes box.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:18-23, 99-101. The job requires naming the duplicate and naming the fields to correct (backend supports revision_fields). The coordinator does not know whether typing '#11' in notes links anything, and later cannot see what they asked for.

frictionPoints.step: Wanting to check or change the GeoTech office
frictionPoints.problem: Nowhere in the two dialogs is the destination GeoTech office shown or overridable.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The domain expects the coordinator to preview 'District 3 -> North office' and rarely override it with a reason; the web flow never mentions an office. The success notice says 'routed for office delegation' without saying which office.

frictionPoints.step: Submit fails (network / 409 because the report was already triaged)
frictionPoints.problem: The error is written to the page banner behind the dark overlay while the dialog stays open, so the coordinator sees a spinner stop and nothing else.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: TriageWorkItem.tsx:43-44 calls onError -> MyWorkPage.tsx:127 renders behind the modal (z-50 overlay). The user re-clicks, then cancels, then discovers a red message they never saw during the dialog.

frictionPoints.problem: Notice text 'assessment #7 routed for office delegation' introduces a new number (assessment id) and a new step name; there is no link to follow it and no dismiss.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: TriageWorkItem.tsx:40; MyWorkPage.tsx:128. The coordinator thinks in incident numbers; 'assessment #7' feels like a different case.

tasks.task: Check what happened to a report I triaged last week
steps: Open My Work — the report is gone because the queue only lists current_stage COORDINATOR_REVIEW (MyWorkPage.tsx:60). Nothing on the page says where triaged items went; the empty-state link points at 'Operations › Assessments' (MyWorkPage.tsx:133).
Guess between 'Incidents', 'Event Groups', 'Assessments' and 'Mission Center' in the sidebar; pick Operations › Incidents.
On /incidents the 'Incident records (N)' tab is active with a grey banner 'Read-only record view. Triage, routing, and assignment actions live in My Work' (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:222, 266-268).

Type the title, county or route into 'Search title, county, route, or description' (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:225) — there is no date filter and no 'triaged by me' filter — and scan the table columns ID / Incident / Location / Status / Assignment / Assessment / Submission (lines 278-283).

Read the row: '#12', title, 'Unclassified · assessment not started', 'Event Group #4', coords + 'D3 · Placer · R080 · PM 12.30', 'View on map', status pill 'New' / 'In progress' / 'Resolved', assignment name or 'Unassigned', and 'AS #7' with a state badge such as 'Pending engineer assignment' or 'No assessment' (lines 300-320).

For more, click 'AS #7' -> /assessments/7 (read-only Assessments record view): six-step pipeline, 'Waiting on <role>', assignments, and history (web/src/features/assessments/AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx per inventory).

If the answer is 'what did I decide and write last week', click 'Event Group #4' -> Event Group history list (web/src/pages/EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:143-145) which shows Event Group events, not the triage disposition or notes.

frictionPoints.problem: Triaged reports vanish from the only page the coordinator knows, with no 'recently triaged' or 'done' section and no hint of where they went.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: MyWorkPage.tsx:59-60 filters to COORDINATOR_REVIEW only; the empty state sends users to Assessments, not Incidents (MyWorkPage.tsx:133). A newcomer's mental model is an inbox with a 'sent/done' folder.

frictionPoints.problem: Incidents, Event Groups, Assessments and Mission Center all plausibly contain 'my report'; the labels do not say which one answers 'what happened to it'.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: AppShell.tsx:84-87 lists them flat with icons only. 'Assessments' and 'Mission Center' are GeoTech-side words; the coordinator does not know an assessment is the downstream object of their 'Assessment required' decision.

frictionPoints.problem: No date, district or 'my decisions' filter; search covers title/county/route/description/id only (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:124-128); up to 1000 rows load into one table.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: A coordinator remembers 'the one on 80 near Colfax last Tuesday', not an id. 'Unclaimed only' (line 232-235) sounds like a filter for their reports but actually means 'no engineer assignment'.

frictionPoints.problem: An accepted report still shows the red 'New' pill (status NEW; only current_stage moved to OFFICE_CHIEF_REVIEW), identical in colour and word to a not-yet-triaged report.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: incidentStatusLabel maps NEW -> 'New' with a red badge (web/src/features/incidents/incidentUiModel.ts:57-70) and the table never shows current_stage (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:311). The coordinator concludes nothing has happened. The Event Group page does show 'New · Office Chief Review' (EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:24-27, 126) — a different answer for the same incident.

frictionPoints.problem: Those dispositions resolve the incident, so the row reads 'Resolved' with no indication it was closed at triage by the coordinator; the disposition and the duplicate target are not displayed anywhere.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: triage_disposition / triage_notes / duplicate_of_incident_id are never rendered on /incidents or /event-groups/:id. 'Resolved' implies the engineer fixed something. The coordinator cannot confirm their own decision was recorded.

frictionPoints.problem: A report sent back to the reporter stays in COORDINATOR_REVIEW, so it is still in My Work as 'New report / Awaiting triage' and on the 'Awaiting intake' tab, with no 'Waiting on reporter' marker.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: MyWorkPage.tsx:60 and IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:119 key off current_stage only; location_match_status NEEDS_REVISION is not surfaced. The coordinator re-opens the item, sees 'Start triage', and either triages it again or believes their earlier request was lost. The domain explicitly needs WAITING_ON_REPORTER vs waiting-on-me.

frictionPoints.step: Classification text in the Incident column
frictionPoints.problem: 'Unclassified · assessment not started' / 'Loading classification…' sits under every title.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: web/src/features/incidents/incidentClassification.ts:18-24. 'Classification' is a GISA outcome; a coordinator reads 'Unclassified' as something they forgot to do.

frictionPoints.problem: 'AS #7' and 'Sub #9' abbreviations, then a page whose pipeline steps are 'Office delegation → Branch assignment → Engineering → Review → Approval → Finalized'.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:315-318 abbreviate; the pipeline is GeoTech-internal vocabulary. The coordinator only wants 'accepted / engineer assigned / done'. The read-only banner on Assessments also tells them to go to My Work, where the item is not.

frictionPoints.step: Looking for the timeline / workflow tree
frictionPoints.problem: No per-incident history or workflow tree is reachable from the web Incidents page; WorkflowTree exists as a component but is not mounted anywhere.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: Grep shows web/src/components/WorkflowTree.tsx has no consumer. The mobile app shows a workflow rail per incident; the desktop shows a flat row.

tasks.task: Find every open incident on I-80 in my district on the map
steps: Look for a map: sidebar has no 'Map' item; guess 'Mission Center' (AppShell.tsx:84) because of the map icon, or click 'View on map' on an Incidents row (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:309), which opens a single incident.

/mission-center loads a statewide map of Event Group markers (blue circles sized by active count) with a right rail 'Event Groups · N shown on map' and toolbar 'Search Event Groups — county, route, post mile…' + status select 'All statuses / Open / Closed / Archived' (web/src/features/missionCenter/MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:240-257, 286-303; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:236-262).

Type '80' into the search (typing 'I-80' or 'R080' matches nothing because the haystack holds the raw route value; web/src/features/missionCenter/missionCenterGisModel.ts:66-79). Set status to 'Open'. There is no district filter, so groups on Route 80 in D3, D4 and D10 all remain.
Read the rail cards ('Event Group #4 · D3 · Placer · R080 · PM 10.80', '3 associated Incidents · 1 active') to pick out the D3 ones by eye (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:296-300).

Click one group. Map zooms to that group's incidents as red diamonds (active) / grey circles (resolved); rail lists 'Associated Incidents' with 'New' / 'In progress' / 'Resolved' pills (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:307-329; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:276-306).
Click '← All California Event Groups' and repeat for every other D3 Route-80 group; the map never shows incidents from more than one group at once.
Alternative: Operations › Incidents, search '80', status 'New'/'In progress', and click 'View on map' on each row — one incident per map view (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:225-231, 309).

frictionPoints.problem: The nav entry is 'Mission Center', not 'Map'; the only other map affordance is a per-row 'View on map' link.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: AppShell.tsx:84 label + generic map icon. 'Mission Center' sounds like a command dashboard for chiefs; a coordinator has no reason to expect a statewide map there.

frictionPoints.problem: The statewide map plots Event Groups, not incidents; incidents only appear after drilling into one group.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:229-263 draws only projects in PROJECTS mode; incidents draw in PROJECT/INCIDENT modes only (lines 265-307). The legend says 'Event Group · Marker size reflects active Incident activity' (line 377). 'Every open incident on I-80' therefore cannot be shown on one screen — the coordinator must open each group in turn and mentally merge them.

frictionPoints.problem: Unclear whether to type 'I-80', '80', '080' or 'R080'; only the raw stored value matches, and '80' also matches post miles, ids and descriptions containing 80.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: missionCenterGisModel.ts:69-78 concatenates id/title/description/district/county/route/post_mile and substring-matches. The displayed label prefixes 'R' (eventGroupTypes.ts:75), so copying what is on screen fails. No route/district dropdowns exist.

frictionPoints.problem: No district filter on Mission Center, Event Groups or Incidents; district is only a 'D3' token inside the location string.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:243-249 offers search + Event Group status only. The coordinator's whole world is one district; having to eyeball 'D3' in dozens of rail cards feels like the software does not know who they are.

frictionPoints.problem: The status filter applies to Event Group status (Open/Closed/Archived), not incident status; an open group can contain only resolved incidents and a closed group is hidden even if it had an in-progress incident.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:205, 244-249. The word 'Open' matches the task wording ('open incident') so the coordinator believes the filter did what they asked.

frictionPoints.step: Reading incident status on the map
frictionPoints.problem: Red diamond = 'Active Incident' (status NEW or IN_PROGRESS) and grey = 'Resolved' (MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:69-73, 378); popups print raw status 'NEW' / 'IN_PROGRESS' (line 297).
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: 'Active' on the map vs 'New'/'In progress' in the rail vs raw enum in the popup — three vocabularies for one attribute.

frictionPoints.problem: The ArcGIS 'Search map' expander on the map is a geocoder for addresses, not an ERIS incident search, but it is the most prominent search on the screen.
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:189-192. A newcomer types 'I-80 Colfax' into it, the map pans to the town, and nothing in ERIS is filtered.

frictionPoints.step: Reports awaiting intake are not on any map
frictionPoints.problem: Untriaged field reports have no Event Group yet, so they appear neither on Mission Center nor via 'View on map' (link only renders when event_group_id is set, IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:309).
frictionPoints.whyConfusing: The coordinator's 'open incidents' include this morning's reports; the map silently omits them.

firstDayConfusions: 'Event Group' is the first thing the coordinator is asked to decide and it is never defined; the job word is 'location/site', mobile says 'Project', and the older URL says /projects (EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:167; App.tsx:77-78).

Two commit buttons in one dialog: 'Record decision · use selected Event Group' (outlined) must be pressed before 'Continue to triage' (primary, disabled with no tooltip) (EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:208-211, 237).
The nearest Event Group is pre-checked, so an unread dialog attaches the report to the closest existing event (EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:92-94).

'Disposition' defaults to 'Assessment required' and commits in one click; a coordinator who only wants to 'accept the report' routes it to GeoTech every time (TriageWorkItem.tsx:75; IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:106).
'Duplicate or linked' and 'Needs reporter information' have no target incident or field picker — only free text (IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:18-23, 99-101).
After triage the report disappears from My Work and reappears on Incidents still labelled 'New' in red, indistinguishable from an untriaged report (MyWorkPage.tsx:60; incidentUiModel.ts:57-70).

A report sent back to the reporter stays in My Work as 'New report / Awaiting triage' with 'Start triage' still offered — the coordinator cannot tell it is waiting on the reporter (MyWorkPage.tsx:60; TriageWorkItem.tsx:59, 73-79).
No photos, reporter identity or incident type anywhere on the web; 'Open incident record' only highlights a table row (TriageWorkItem.tsx:63; IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:102-112).
Errors during triage render behind the modal overlay, so a failed submit looks like nothing happened (TriageWorkItem.tsx:43-44; MyWorkPage.tsx:127).
The map ('Mission Center') shows Event Groups statewide, not incidents, and has no district or route filter (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:240-257; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:229-263).
Route search needs the raw value ('80'), while the screen displays 'R080' and the coordinator says 'I-80' (missionCenterGisModel.ts:66-79; eventGroupTypes.ts:75).
Header shows the raw role code 'MAINT_COORDINATOR' and the sidebar offers GeoTech-only areas (Assessments, Terrain Cross Sections) with no hint they are not for this role (AppShell.tsx:87, 91, 157).
The step-2 dialog explains 'permanent Incident key is minted' and 'classification remains unassigned' — engineering internals the coordinator thinks they must act on (IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:85).

Vocabulary churn for one state: 'New report' / 'Awaiting triage' / 'not yet in the incident record' / 'Awaiting intake' (MyWorkPage.tsx:153; TriageWorkItem.tsx:55, 59; IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:223).
mentalModelGaps: Job: 'a report comes in, I accept it or send it back'. Software: a two-object commit (Event Group association persisted first, disposition second) where the first save is irreversible and precedes the decision the coordinator actually cares about (EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:140-146; IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:71-79).

Job: 'link the report to the location so history stays together'. Software: 'Event Group' with a 25-mile radius list — a spatial grouping of events, not the location record the domain describes (GET location-candidates / location-link are not what the web dialog calls); the coordinator has no way to know whether the group is the slope, the storm or the route segment.

Job: incidents have one plain status (new / accepted / with GeoTech / engineer on it / done / sent back). Software: incident.status (NEW/IN_PROGRESS/RESOLVED) and current_stage (COORDINATOR_REVIEW / OFFICE_CHIEF_REVIEW / …) are separate, the web Incidents page shows only the first, and an accepted report and an untriaged report both read 'New' (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:311; EventGroupDetailPage.tsx:24-27).

Job: 'my district'. Software: role-scoped queues and statewide record pages with no district concept in any filter; district exists only as a 'D3' fragment in a location string (eventGroupTypes.ts:71-79).

Job: 'the report' is one thing with a history. Software: incident -> assessment -> submission are three numbered objects ('#12', 'AS #7', 'Sub #9') across three pages, and the coordinator's own triage decision and notes are stored but never shown back (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:315-318).
Job: 'no assessment needed' or 'duplicate' means 'filed, nothing more to do'. Software: those dispositions mark the incident RESOLVED, which reads as 'fixed by someone' (incidentUiModel.ts:59).

Job: 'map of my open incidents'. Software: a drill-down of Event Groups -> one group's incidents -> one incident's photos, designed for GIS evidence review, not for a district picture (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:94-98).

Job: routing to a GeoTech office is a visible hand-off. Software: the office is computed server-side and never shown or overridable in the web triage flow; the notice only says 'routed for office delegation' (TriageWorkItem.tsx:40).
topFixes: Merge the two triage modals into one screen with a single primary 'Accept report' commit: Event Group choice (radio list + map) on the left, disposition + notes on the right, and no server write until the final button; if association must persist separately, make the current 'Record decision' the primary button and hide 'Continue' until it is done (EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:208-237; IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:71-108).

Do not pre-select the nearest Event Group; show it as 'Suggested · 1.5 mi away' with an explicit choice, and add a one-line definition of Event Group ('one real-world event or site; several reports can attach to it') in the dialog header (EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx:92-94, 168).

Give the triage panel the evidence the decision needs: reporter photos (thumbnails), reporter name/contact, incident type and the road-inventory match card, and turn 'Open incident record' into a real incident detail page instead of a highlighted table row (TriageWorkItem.tsx:52-65; IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:102-112).

Make disposition an explicit choice: no default (or default 'No assessment required'), radio buttons with consequence text instead of a select, and a target-incident picker for 'Duplicate or linked' plus a field checklist for 'Needs reporter information' (TriageWorkItem.tsx:75; IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:18-23, 93-101).

Show workflow position, not raw status, on the Incidents table and rail: replace the red 'New' pill for accepted reports with 'Accepted · with North GeoTech office', 'Engineer assigned · <name>', 'Closed at triage · No assessment' / 'Duplicate of #11', and 'Waiting on reporter' — driven by current_stage, triage_disposition and location_match_status (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:311; incidentUiModel.ts:57-70).

Split My Work for coordinators into 'Needs my decision', 'Waiting on reporter' and 'Recently triaged (7 days)' so sent-back and just-accepted reports do not vanish or masquerade as new (MyWorkPage.tsx:59-72).

Add district and route filters (and a 'My district' default) to Incidents, Event Groups and Mission Center, normalise route search so '80', '080', 'I-80' and 'R080' all match, and add an 'All incidents in view' layer to the Mission Center map so open incidents can be seen across groups (MissionCenterProjectExplorer.tsx:240-257; missionCenterGisModel.ts:66-79; MissionCenterProjectGisMap.tsx:229-307).
Render errors inside the open dialog (and keep the button re-enabled) instead of in the page banner behind the overlay (TriageWorkItem.tsx:43-44; MyWorkPage.tsx:127).

Show the computed GeoTech office in the disposition step ('Will be routed to North GeoTech Office · change…') with the reason field the backend already requires for overrides, and link the success notice to the incident row (IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:82-108; TriageWorkItem.tsx:40).

Humanise the shell for this role: 'Maintenance Coordinator · District 3' instead of 'MAINT_COORDINATOR' in the header, one label for the pre-intake state everywhere ('Awaiting intake'), and remove the key-minting/classification policy paragraph from the triage dialog (AppShell.tsx:157; MyWorkPage.tsx:153; TriageWorkItem.tsx:55, 59; IncidentDecisionDialogs.tsx:85).
